problem_checks.decisive_check: Actually viewed source physical pages6/15 (printed1496/1505) and read the Section4.1 assumptions on physical14. Before(2.7), both flow endpoints and the node sum are restricted to Lambda_N although rho is outside. Summing the displayed divergence over finite Lambda_N gives zero by antisymmetry on the left and one on the right. In(4.9), the diagonal sum is explicitly over k in Lambda, so the literal internal Laplacian annihilates the constant vector. The admissible finite singleton Lambda={i}, h_i=2, exp(u_i)=3, u_rho=0 has connected positive-weight extended graph, but the printed Dii is0 whereas the intended grounded Dii is6. These are exact algebraic checks under the actual assumptions, not numerical near-singularity tests.
problem_checks.counterevidence_and_scope: Equations(2.7)-(2.9) already sum over all E_N, including wiring edges. Immediately after(4.9) the source explicitly adds h_i exp(u_i);(4.11) removes the rho row of the incidence matrix but explicitly keeps pinning-edge columns, and(4.13) gives D=F W F^T. Including rho in incident sums yields v^T D v=sum_internal W_ij exp(u_i+u_j)(v_i-v_j)^2+sum_i h_i exp(u_i)v_i^2. Connectedness to rho means each internal component has positive pinning, so this form is strictly positive for nonzero v. These adjacent intended objects remove the two displayed obstructions; no invalid intended core derivation or counterexample to the transience/moment theorems is established. Minor is appropriately scoped.
